biography.html: Edward Samuel Rogers Jr., known as Ted, was the Canadian founder and chief executive of Rogers Communications. He built the Toronto business from radio into cable television, wireless services and publishing. Trained in law at Osgoode Hall, he followed his inventor father's interest in communications and supported hospitals and universities with his wife, Loretta.

long_biography.plain_text:
When Ted Rogers bought CHFI, few Toronto households owned an FM receiver. He persuaded Westinghouse Canada to make inexpensive radios, which he sold or gave away to help build an audience. The move tackled a practical obstacle: listeners needed suitable equipment before they could hear the station's programmes.

His business card described him as a senior salesperson. Rogers sought ideas from engineers, customer service staff and customers he met on the street. When his company's board rejected an early move into cellular telephony, he found partners and invested his own money. He later bought out those partners, establishing another major part of the communications business.

confidence.reason: Full company founder biography and St James Press business history support the concrete marketing method, listening habits and personally funded cellular initiative.
